text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
SUGAR - World market for March 5, 1997

White sugar futures in London closed lower in quiet trade. There was no fresh news to influence prices. May was down 90 cents to close at $307.20 per tonne, while August gave up $1.60 to close at $305.50 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed lower across the board with front month March loosing 2 points to close at 10.86 cents/lb, while July ended 4 points lower at 10.67 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 6 and 9 points. The dockworkers' strike at Brazil's port of Paranagua had, as anticipated, no effect on sugar prices.
FUNDAMENTALS

CUBA - Vice President Carlos Lage confirmed, that Cuban sugar production in 1996/97 will only be slightly up on last year's 4.530 million tonnes, raw value. Lage said production at the end of February was more or less 2 million tonnes, which compares to roughly 1.8 million tonnes the same period in 1995/96.

Lage added the 1996/97 harvest had begun late, largely because of delays in foreign financing, which he attributed to the Helms-Burton act. He said the measure, which seeks to curb foreign investment in Cuba initially interrupted foreign financing. Lage emphasized another difficulty was dry weather during the past summer, as well as damage in some areas from Hurricane Lili, which swept across parts of the country in October. In our last world balance estimate we had put Cuban sugar production in 1996/97 at 4.7 million tonnes.

BRAZIL - Brazilian sugar production is seen remaining at 13 million tonnes, tel quel, in 1997/98, the same level as in 1996/97, Mauricio Assis, the head of the Industry and Commerce Ministry's primary commodities department said. He added that sugar cane production in the south was expected to grow by 5 per cent in 1997/98 from this year's level and productivity by 1.2 per cent.

But Assis said, next year's extra cane production would be used for more alcohol production. Industry sources recently estimated that the cane crop in the Center South could rise by at least 5 per cent or an additional 10 to 15 million tonnes. Assis said alcohol production in 1997/98 could reach 15 billion litres against 14 billion litres the previous year.
He added the increase will remove the need to import alcohol in 1997/98 compared to an estimated 375 million litres in 1996/97, significantly below earlier forecasts of 560 million litres.
UNITED STATES - Industry analysts expect the USDA supply demand report, due next week, not to trigger the cancellation of the March quota allocation of 200,000 tonnes.

The increase would bring the total tariff rate quota for 1996/97 up to 1.9 million tonnes, raw value. Under a new formula for managing the quota, the USDA initially allocated just 1.7 million tonnes, with further allocations of 200,000 tonnes each due in January, March and May depending on the projected stocks to use ratio for 1996/97, not exceeding 15.5 per cent in each of those months.

In February the USDA calculated the stocks to use ratio at 14.6 per cent and industry observers do not expect any major revision in next week's supply/demand sheet so that the increase in the tariff rate quota is likely to go ahead.

NETHERLANDS - Sugar exports in November 1996 amounted to 36,600 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 12,247 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first two months of 1996/97 (October/November) up to 46,840 tonnes compared to 81,383 tonnes in October/November 1995.
Total exports in 1995/96 reached 301,918 tonnes compared to 381,586 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in October/November 1996 was Algeria with 28,123 tonnes whites against nil.

Sugar imports in October/November 1996 amounted to 12,583 tonnes against 13,100 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 59,658 tonnes against 64,568 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/November 1996 were France with 5,786 tonnes whites against 6,152 tonnes and Belgium-Luxembourg with 3,940 tonnes compared to 3,207 tonnes.

ROMANIA - Sugar production in December 1996 amounted to 30,250 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 22,672 tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first four months of 1996/97 (September/December) up to 245,878 tonnes against 217,421 tonnes in 1995/96. Total production in 1995/96 was 217,653 tonnes compared to 206,614 tonnes in 1994/95.

Sugar imports in December 1996 reached 10,190 tonnes compared to 15,470 tonnes in December 1995. This brought cumulative imports in September/December 1996 up to 141,966 tonnes against 56,860 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 327,159 tonnes compared to 275,178 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in September/December 1996 were Brazil with 83,499 tonnes whites against 21,000 tonnes, Moldova with 12,201 tonnes compared to 9,182 tonnes and Austria with 10,115 tonnes, up from 5,491 tonnes.
TENDERS

The European Union awarded 34,750 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 43.835 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on March 5. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to March 5 reached 1,597,900 tonnes, which compares to 1,603,198 tonnes last year.
